question: Why did h33-h33-2-b2 score 0.2778, and can it be beaten from this workspace?

calibration.family: five binary isolated-dot artifacts of one family, 37,654 <= n <= 61,328 dots, all with 0 pixels on the public catalogue
calibration.model: score(n) = T / (0.2*n + 0.8*K_eff), where T is the triangular-kernel credit of the artifact measured against USGS SGMC faults absent from the competition catalogue
calibration.verdict: one fitted constant reproduces five live leaderboard scores to RMSE 0.0045 -- half a leaderboard point. The credit T is therefore a *transferable* measurement inside this family, and it is measurable here without the organizers' labels.

failure.artifact: h19-5 powerlaw-budget family member with n=91,533
failure.detail: Fitting K on all six artifacts (K=24,707) leaves RMSE 0.1125 and mis-ranks the 91,533-dot artifact above the 37,654-dot one. Both fits under-predict the mass penalty at large n: every instrument available here is one-sided because it cannot see the organizers' hidden truth.
failure.consequence: the calibrated model may only be used inside 37,654 <= n <= 61,328 dots, and any count above that window is refused by this workspace's own evidence.

field.definition: 0.85 * |l1-l2| structure-tensor anisotropy of the detrended-elevation band (sigma 1.5/3/6 px) + 0.15 * fault-tip extrapolation, normalised to [0,1]

same_n_credit.note: interpolated between the measured 35,000 and 45,000 points

count_rule.instrument_A: credit model at K_eff=15,303: below n=27,000 this field projects under the group best 0.2778 (n=24,000 -> 0.245; n=20,000 -> 0.223), above it the projection rises (n=28,000 -> 0.2937)
count_rule.instrument_B: ledger mass slope measured within the same family (44,090 -> 37,654 dots removed 6,436, score +0.0178): every dot above ~38,000 is priced against us
count_rule.caveat: both are ESTIMATES from instruments that are one-sided against mass; neither is a receipt. The only scored receipt in this repository is 0.2778 (user-reported).

pass4_blend.field: norm(score^2-weighted consensus of 16 live-scored artifacts) + norm(curvature ridge)

consensus_alone.verdict: the group's own best live-scored artifacts are a WORSE proxy for the official SGMC off-catalogue population than a plain elevation-curvature ridge; their value is complementary, not authoritative

projection.caveat: both estimators inherit the SGMC-to-hidden-truth transfer assumption, which no instrument in this workspace can validate
